summary.one_liner: Amplifier is Microsoft's early-preview, modular AI development assistant, with a Python command-line app as its reference interface.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a CLI (amplifier) for chatting with AI models, running one-off prompts, and generating or debugging code. Behavior is organized into composable "bundles" that define tools, providers, agents, and behaviors, and users can add or switch them. Specialized agents such as zen-architect, bug-hunter, web-research, modular-builder, and explorer can be delegated tasks. Sessions are saved automatically and scoped per project, so they can be listed, shown, resumed, or continued. The README also mentions a web-based log viewer for debugging sessions, and a modular core (amplifier-core) and foundation library for building custom modules.
use_cases: debug errors with an AI agent
switch between Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or local Ollama models
how_to_run: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh  (macOS/Linux/WSL; URL was stripped in the README text, so this is inferred from the standard uv installer)
uv tool install git+https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier  (URL truncated in the README)
notable: Modular bundle system: swap providers, tools, agents, and behaviors like building blocks
Built-in agents for design, debugging, research, and code implementation
Project-scoped session persistence with resume and continue commands
Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI (including Azure CLI auth), and local Ollama models
Ships a web-based log viewer with real-time streaming and JSON inspection
caveats: Explicitly a research demonstrator in early preview; APIs may change and safety systems are not yet built in
Tested primarily on macOS, Linux, and WSL; native Windows shells have known issues
Most testing done with Anthropic Claude; other providers may have rough edges
Not currently accepting external contributions per the README
